ak-asu/cloudforge.title: CloudForge — PRD-to-Production Cloud Infrastructure Generator
ak-asu/cloudforge.summary: CloudForge is a full-stack platform that turns a plain-English PRD into deployed AWS infrastructure. Rather than letting an LLM invent an architecture, it grounds every decision in a knowledge graph of validated cloud patterns and uses the LLM only to explain what the graph derived. The pipeline runs in four streamed stages: (1) PRD refinement — a LangGraph agent (agent1) extracts non-functional requirements, optionally researches via web search, and asks up to 6 rounds of multi-choice clarifying questions (2–4 options + freeform, GitHub-Copilot-planning-mode style) before emitting structured requirements JSON; (2) architecture planning — a second LangGraph graph (architecture_planner) chains seven specialised sub-agents (service discovery, load simulation, resilience/blast-radius simulation, compliance mapping for SOC 2/HIPAA/ISO 27001, deterministic architecture tests) with a human-in-the-loop accept/reject gate via LangGraph interrupts, auto-retrying up to 3 times on CRITICAL violations; (3) code & Terraform generation — a multi-subgraph LangGraph pipeline (agent3) with an orchestrator, TF generator, TF validation loop (TFLint + Checkov + terraform validate with auto-fix retries), per-service code/test generation, and an assembler, producing main.tf/variables.tf/outputs.tf plus application code; (4) deploy — CloudFormation provisioning via temporary STS AssumeRole credentials, with generated code committed to the user's GitHub repo via GitHub App OAuth. The backend is FastAPI (Python 3.12) with Motor/MongoDB persistence, Fernet-encrypted (AES-128-CBC) credential storage, JWT auth, and full-pipeline Server-Sent Events streaming across routers (prd, architecture_sse, build, deploy, files, history, workflows, auth). A provider factory (providers/factory.py) renders an intermediate topology graph into provider-specific IaC — AWS is live, with GCP and Azure cost fetchers already implemented in a registry pattern. The frontend is Next.js 15 with a React Flow cloud canvas (drag-and-drop AWS nodes, topology export), Zustand stores, and a shared TypeScript topology schema package (@cloudforge/types) that serves as the contract between the canvas and the backend Terraform generator. Prompt engineering is templated via Jinja2 across all agents, and the repo includes integration tests for the full agent3 pipeline, knowledge-graph/RAG retrieval, and the Terraform MCP adapter.
ak-asu/cloudforge.readme: CloudForge — From product requirements to live AWS infrastructure — graph-validated, Terraform-provisioned, GitHub-committed. Hackathon project by Aakash Khepar, Bhavya Nimesh Shah, Aditya Jindal, and Gunbhir.

ak-asu/energyhackathon.title: COLLIDE — AI-Powered BTM Data Center Site Selection
ak-asu/energyhackathon.summary: COLLIDE is a full-stack platform for scoring behind-the-meter (BTM) natural-gas data center sites across Texas and the Southwest, built for the ASU Energy Hackathon 2026. Hyperscale AI data centers need 50–500 MW of co-located 24/7 power, and with grid interconnection queues stretching 3–7 years, BTM gas generation is the practical alternative — but siting requires evaluating land viability, gas supply reliability, and power economics that are normally assessed in silos. The system scores any coordinate across all three constraints simultaneously and streams a composite scorecard with 20-year NPV estimates, plus a natural-language AI analyst for what-if questions against live market data.

bhavyashah1234/agenticreportgeneration.title: Agentic Reports — Snowflake-connected agentic report generation platform
bhavyashah1234/agenticreportgeneration.summary: Built Agentic Reports, a full-stack agentic report-generation platform that connects to a company's Snowflake warehouse and turns natural-language prompts and drag-and-drop design into client-specific PDF reports. The core idea is a safety-first agent architecture: an open-weight LLM (Snowflake Cortex `llama3.1-70b` by default, with automatic fallback to local Ollama `qwen3:8b`) never writes raw SQL — it selects from 9 builtin 'archetypes' (aggregate, time_series, top_n, share_of_total, period_over_period, kpi_summary, moving_average, pivot, distribution) and their parameters, which compile to parameterised Snowflake SQL with values bound rather than concatenated. Companies can also define custom archetypes as either parameterised presets of builtins or read-only SQL templates validated with sqlglot. The backend is FastAPI (Python 3.14) with SQLModel/SQLite for app metadata, snowflake-connector-python, pandas, and Playwright for headless-Chromium PDF rendering; routes cover auth (company workspaces keyed by email domain, encrypted Snowflake Programmatic Access Tokens), connection management, schema catalog, archetypes, formats, runs (with full report snapshots and run history), and the agent. The frontend is Next.js 16 / React 19 with a 12-column drag-and-drop canvas (react-grid-layout v2, Recharts 3, zustand) offering 11 widget types (KPI, table, bar, stacked bar, line, area, pie, donut, scatter, text, heading) with live Snowflake data during editing, runtime parameter declarations (client, period), and a print page for PDF generation. The agent handles both single-widget requests ('show quarterly revenue by territory as a stacked bar') and full report drafting, plus executive-summary narratives at generation time. Includes a pytest suite (unit tests for archetype SQL compilation, injection resistance, and bind-parameter safety, plus API tests for auth, agent, connections, formats, preview, and runs), a Makefile-driven dev workflow, and demo-hosting scripts that expose the app through a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel while running all public queries under a least-privilege read-only Snowflake role (DEMO_READER). Built for MLH Hacktoberfest x Sunhacks.
bhavyashah1234/agenticreportgeneration.readme: The README is thorough and specific: it documents the product (Snowflake-connected agentic report generation), the 9 builtin archetypes, the LLM provider strategy (Snowflake Cortex with Ollama fallback), the stack table, the demo dataset, and local-run instructions. It also candidly documents operational caveats (Cortex blocked on trial accounts, network-policy requirements for PATs).

forgeopus/visionforge.title: VisionForge — Visual Neural Network Builder with Multi-Framework Code Export
forgeopus/visionforge.summary: VisionForge is a full-stack visual neural network builder that turns drag-and-drop layer graphs into production-ready PyTorch/TensorFlow training code. A React 19 + TypeScript canvas (ReactFlow, Zustand, shadcn/ui) lets users wire ~25 layer types into a dataflow graph; a Django REST backend runs a Kahn's-algorithm topological shape-inference engine that propagates tensor shapes through the graph, validates the architecture (config, connection, and acyclicity rules), and generates multi-file training projects (model/train/dataset/config) from framework-specific Jinja2 templates via PyTorch and TensorFlow codegen orchestrators. An AI assistant layer (Gemini + Claude behind a service factory) accepts natural-language requests with the live workflow state to answer questions or modify the model. Supporting systems include Firebase auth with guest mode, project persistence and sharing, group blocks for reusable sub-modules, and CI with CodeQL scanning and Claude-powered code review.
forgeopus/visionforge.readme: VisionForge is a visual neural network builder: users drag-and-drop layer blocks on a canvas, connect them into a dataflow graph, configure parameters, validate the architecture, and export production-ready PyTorch or TensorFlow training code. It targets researchers, students, and ML engineers who want to prototype architectures without hand-writing boilerplate.
results: Built a full-stack no-code deep-learning tool: a React 19 + TypeScript canvas (ReactFlow, Zustand, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Framer Motion) where users assemble ~25 layer types (Conv1D/2D/3D, Linear, LSTM, GRU, Embedding, Attention, BatchNorm, pooling, Add/Concat merge ops, Loss, Metrics, custom layers) into model graphs, with undo/redo, group blocks, project dashboards, and shareable read-only canvases.

Implemented an automatic tensor-shape inference engine on the backend: builds an adjacency list from the node/edge graph, topologically sorts it with Kahn's algorithm (rejecting cyclic graphs), and propagates input/output shapes node-by-node so users never track dimensions manually; per-layer shape rules (conv, pool, linear, flatten, concat, add, batchnorm) live in a dedicated rules module.

Designed a dual-framework code-generation pipeline: framework-specific node specs (PyTorch NCHW vs TensorFlow NHWC, e.g. nn.Linear vs layers.Dense) feed Jinja2 templates that render multi-file training projects (model.py, train.py, dataset.py, config.py) via PyTorch and TensorFlow orchestrators, including group-block generators for composite/residual sub-modules.

Integrated AI assistance with a pluggable provider architecture: an AI service factory dispatches to Google Gemini and Anthropic Claude backends, and a chat endpoint accepts natural-language messages plus the current workflow state (nodes/edges) and optional file uploads, returning model modifications; users supply their own API keys via headers (X-Gemini-Api-Key / X-Anthropic-Api-Key).

Built real-time architecture validation (config, connection, acyclicity, single-input, and multi-input checks) surfaced in a frontend ValidationErrorsPanel, plus Firebase authentication with middleware, guest mode, idle-timeout handling, and encrypted API-key storage on the frontend.
